A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe the same two-hand reconstruction framework, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither includes a separate appendix. Although v3 mentions an appendix, its dataset and metric details remain in Sections 4.2–4.3.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction results on InterHand2.6M, HIC and FreiHAND, component ablations, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original reconstruction results and ablations, and adds efficiency measurements, penetration metrics and diffusion-refinement examples.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives, diffusion conditioning and collision-guided inference remain substantially the same. However, v2 explicitly averages prior features before projection, whereas v3 Equation 1 writes Proj(Fk, Fs, Fd) without specifying aggregation. The PDFs do not establish whether fusion changed or its description was merely abbreviated.

E1.justification: Both versions explicitly specify the same five training datasets and testing on InterHand2.6M, FreiHAND and HIC. Re:InterHand and real-scene qualitative coverage also remain. v3 removes the FreiHAND results but retains its stated testing use; the added analyses introduce no distinct dataset or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds InterHandGen to the InterHand2.6M comparison and evaluates it in the new penetration and qualitative comparisons. The entire standalone FreiHAND comparison against METRO, MeshGraphormer, AMVUR, HaMeR and Zhou et al. disappears. This substantially revises the reported comparison coverage, while the other main comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation using penetration volume, penetration distance and proximity ratio, plus parameter-count and FPS comparisons of foundation-encoder, fusion-encoder and diffusion configurations. Existing dataset splits, reconstruction metrics, training settings and the InterHand2.6M 5fps protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cumulative prior/diffusion ablation is unchanged after moving from v2 Table 4 to v3 Table 3. v3 substantially extends component validation with an encoder efficiency comparison, direct penetration measurements and three before/after-diffusion case studies with InterHandGen comparisons (Tables 4–5 and Figure 4).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained reconstruction and ablation values are unchanged, including InterHand2.6M MRRPE/MPJPE/MPVPE of 21.60/5.36/5.58 and HIC values of 22.24/6.67/6.93. v3 adds InterHandGen results, configuration-specific speeds of 3/56/18 FPS, and penetration results including PenVol 0.11 versus InterHandGen's 0.76. It removes FreiHAND results and the foundation-inference rows from Tables 1–2. The new foundation-encoder result excludes diffusion and is not a same-setting replacement for those deleted rows.

T1.justification: The added total-loss and diffusion-loss equations formalize objectives already described in v2, and the collision equations are unchanged. However, Equation 1 replaces explicit averaging with an unspecified multivariate projection; whether this changes the mathematical definition or merely abbreviates it is unresolved. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 introduces explicit first-attempt claims for heterogeneous-prior unification and penetration-free two-hand diffusion. Its abstract narrows the performance statement to InterHand2.6M and HIC and emphasizes penetration suppression, although the contribution list still claims FreiHAND superiority. The central two-stage contribution remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation attributing depth-scale ambiguity handling to Sapiens and interprets the new efficiency comparison as an optimal balance. It removes v2's extreme-occlusion limitation, retaining motion blur, and drops the qualification that overlapping-hand segmentation does not distinguish left from right.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the future code-release promise with a project link and identifies an RTX 3090 for the new efficiency measurements. It removes explicit left-hand flipping and reversal instructions. Backbone, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training GPUs and diffusion schedule details remain. The PDFs alone do not establish code availability.

R1.justification: v3 retains the earlier references and adds three generative-motion works: conditional-GAN gesture generation, HuTuMotion and ReinDiffuse. It also makes more explicit contrasts with InterHandGen's regularization and Zuo et al.'s interaction features, alongside stronger priority claims. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten around 2D alignment and 3D plausibility. Method explanations and subsection terminology are extensively revised, experimental discussion is condensed and reorganized, and author affiliations are added. This is substantial narrative editing beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 removes v2's duplicated pipeline figure and revises the remaining diagram. It removes the FreiHAND table, adds efficiency and penetration tables and a diffusion-comparison figure, and relocates the retained ablation table. Existing qualitative figures are resized and renumbered, substantially reorganizing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 and Figure 4 provide direct evidence for efficiency and penetration suppression that v2 lacked, strengthening the central two-hand reconstruction argument and its comparison with InterHandGen. The gain is limited by removal of FreiHAND and foundation-inference evidence, retained FreiHAND claims without their supporting table, and reduced disclosure of occlusion limitations. Core reconstruction accuracy is unchanged.
